proposals.before: You squandered grain to move the gods, you pried with reed stalks for omens; you spurned the spirit's warning— and threw your life into the shallows!
proposals.after: You squandered grain to move the gods, you pried with reed stalks for omens; you spurned Ling Fen's counsel and would not follow— and threw your life into the shallows!
proposals.reason: Focus Chinese has 違靈氛而不從: the named diviner Ling Fen and the refusal to follow. Idiomatic 'the spirit's warning' erases that name; the proposed wording restores both 靈氛 and 而不從 without adding unsupported sense.

proposals.before: Clear and turbid, high and low notes answer one another like masters tuning a flawless lute.
proposals.after: Clear and turbid, high and low notes answer one another like Kui and Boya tuning a flawless lute.
proposals.reason: Chinese 若夔、牙之調琴 names the musicians Kui and Ya (Boya). Replacing generic 'masters' with those names corrects a real omission; the rest of the idiomatic line is unchanged.

proposals.before: The ancient master-builders lay down their tools; the surveyor drops his cord and square.
proposals.after: Ban and Chui cast aside their adze and chisel; Wang Er casts aside his hook and line.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 般、倕 and 王爾 with their tools 剞厥 and 鉤繩. The idiomatic generics drop those persons; Ban, Chui, and Wang Er with adze, chisel, hook, and line match the source.

proposals.before: Xihe guides the day; the groom holds the reins; winds lash; spirits seem to race alongside.
proposals.after: Xihe guides the day; Yanlun holds the reins; winds lash; spirits seem to race alongside.
proposals.reason: Chinese pairs 羲和司日 with 顏倫奉輿. Idiomatic 'the groom' erases Yanlun; naming him restores the parallel personal reference without inventing new content.

proposals.before: They drift Pengli, gaze toward Shun's land, tally night-shining pearls, split moon-pearls, summon river goddesses, feast the drowned poets' shades.
proposals.after: They float across Lake Pengli and gaze toward Youyu; they hammer night-shining crystal, split the wombs of moon-bright pearls, whip Lady Fu of the Luo, and offer a feast to Qu Yuan, Peng Xian, and Wu Zixu.
proposals.reason: Commentaries identify 彭 as Peng Xian and 胥 as Wu Zixu. The original draft erased the names, while the prior review mistakenly fused the two men as 'Peng-Xu'; the corrected wording restores all three recipients and the concrete poetic actions.

proposals.before: They float Lake Pengli, sight Youyu, square the wheel of night-gleaming pearls, split the moon-bright pearl's core, whip Lady Fu of the Luo, feast Qu Yuan and Peng and Xu.
proposals.after: They float on Lake Pengli and gaze toward Youyu; they hammer night-shining crystal, split the wombs of moon-bright pearls, whip Lady Fu of the Luo, and offer a feast to Qu Yuan, Peng Xian, and Wu Zixu.
proposals.reason: Commentaries identify 彭 as Peng Xian and 胥 as Wu Zixu; the draft's 'Peng and Xu' fails to recover either name, while 'wheel' is not present in 方椎.
